domains.title: Procurement Principles, Frameworks & Practical Tools
domains.summary: Governs public buying guidelines under General Financial Rules (GFR 2017) and Government e-Marketplace (GeM), shifting from rudimentary lowest-cost (L1) selection to Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) tailored for algorithmic health systems.
keyStatutes: GFR 2017 Rule 144 (Fundamental principles of public buying)
GFR 2017 Rule 149 (Mandatory GeM procurement)
GFR 2017 Rule 192 (Quality and Cost Based Selection - QCBS)
Department of Expenditure Manual for Procurement of Goods & Services (2022)
internationalGuidance: WHO Guidance on Ethics and Governance of AI for Health (2021) - Chapter 5
NHS England / NICE Evidence Standards Framework (ESF) for Digital Health Technologies
OECD Recommendation of the Council on Public Procurement (2015)
criticalRisks: Unmitigated L1 commodity bidding leading to brittle algorithms with high clinical failure rates.
Opaque bidding specifications that unfairly favor single multinational hardware vendors.
Absence of pre-award computational bench testing on local clinical samples.
recommendedClauses: The evaluation shall follow a Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS 80:20) methodology, wherein bidders must achieve a minimum qualifying technical benchmark of 75 marks before commercial opening.
Mandatory live sandboxed bench testing shall be conducted on an anonymized state-provided clinical validation test set prior to final contract award.

domains.title: Clinical & Technical Performance Validation
domains.summary: Mandates empirical verification of diagnostic accuracy (Sensitivity, Specificity, AUROC, F1 Score) against robust clinical gold standards, with explicit subgroup parity testing across diverse Indian demographic cohorts.
keyStatutes: ICMR Ethical Guidelines for Application of AI in Biomedical Research and Healthcare (2023)
CDSCO Guidance on Clinical Evaluation of Medical Devices and SaMD
Strategy for AI in Healthcare for India (SAHI) - NITI Aayog
internationalGuidance: US FDA AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device Action Plan
TRIPOD-AI & CONSORT-AI Reporting Guidelines
WHO Regulatory Considerations on AI for Health (2023)
criticalRisks: Laboratory overfitting: Vendor claims based solely on clean western academic benchmarks.
High false-positive rate swamping public health laboratory confirmatory capacity (e.g. CBNAAT/TrueNat).
Severe diagnostic drop-offs in rural populations, geriatric cohorts, or pediatric patients.
recommendedClauses: The AI solution must demonstrate a minimum verified Sensitivity of 90.0% and Specificity of 85.0% for screening workflows, evaluated against double-blind specialist consensus.
Bidder must submit a formal Clinical Evaluation Report (CER) including subgroup disaggregated performance metrics across gender, age brackets, and key comorbidities.

domains.title: Safety, Fairness, Equity & Human Oversight
domains.summary: Ensures artificial intelligence acts as assistive decision-support rather than autonomous clinical authority, mandating human-in-the-loop safeguards, bias auditing, and graceful failure fallbacks.
keyStatutes: Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act (2010)
National Medical Commission (Professional Conduct) Regulations
NITI Aayog Responsible AI for All (Approach Documents 1 & 2)
internationalGuidance: EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) - High-Risk Health Systems Requirements
ISO 14971: Application of risk management to medical devices
IEEE 7000 Series Standards on Algorithmic Bias & Ethical Design
criticalRisks: Autonomous algorithmic diagnostic decisions without qualified medical officer validation.
System crashes or silent freezes when cellular networks drop in remote primary health centres.
Algorithmic discrimination against tribal or marginalized socio-economic communities.
recommendedClauses: Human-in-the-Loop Safeguard: The software shall strictly operate in an assistive capacity; the final clinical diagnosis, referral, or prescription shall solely rest with the registered medical practitioner.

Deterministic Fallback Mode: In the event of system error, edge computing failure, or network disruption, the system shall seamlessly revert to manual diagnostic workflow without loss of patient records.

domains.title: Data Governance, Privacy (DPDP) & Cybersecurity
domains.summary: Enforces strict statutory adherence to the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023, ABDM Health Data Management Policy, sovereign data localization, and CERT-In cybersecurity mandates.
keyStatutes: Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 (Act No. 22 of 2023)
ABDM Health Data Management Policy (HDMP)
Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) Cyber Security Directions
internationalGuidance: ISO/IEC 27001 (Information Security Management)
HIPAA Security & Privacy Rules (Comparative Benchmark)
GDPR Health Data Safeguards (Art. 9)
criticalRisks: Transmission of unencrypted citizen health records to foreign or un-empanelled commercial cloud servers.
Unauthorized vendor harvesting of public health telemetry for secondary commercial model training.
Ransomware vulnerabilities in unpatched legacy edge deployment terminals.
recommendedClauses: Data Sovereignty & Localization: All patient data, model inference inputs, telemetry, and audit logs shall be hosted strictly within the territory of India on MeitY-empanelled Cloud Service Providers (CSPs).

Zero Unauthorized Secondary Use: The vendor is explicitly prohibited from utilizing public health datasets or patient telemetry for secondary training or commercialization without explicit state authorization.

domains.title: Interoperability & National Standards (ABDM)
domains.summary: Mandates complete alignment with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) architecture, HL7 FHIR Release 4 schemas, DICOM 3.0 imaging standards, and standardized clinical terminologies.
keyStatutes: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) Architecture v1.0
National Digital Health Blueprint (NDHB) - MoHFW
National Health Stack Specifications (NITI Aayog)
internationalGuidance: HL7 FHIR Release 4 (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources)
DICOM PS 3.1 - 3.20 (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine)
SNOMED CT International & LOINC terminologies
criticalRisks: Proprietary vendor data formats creating acute vendor lock-in and isolated data silos.
Inability to link patient screenings with Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA).
Incompatibility with existing state Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS).
recommendedClauses: ABDM Milestone Compliance: The solution must possess active sandbox certification for ABDM Milestones M1 (ABHA Creation/Verification), M2 (HFR/HPR registration), and M3 (FHIR R4 Health Information Exchange).
Open Interoperability: Medical imaging feeds must natively ingest and export DICOM 3.0 compliant files without requiring proprietary encoding or conversion dongles.

domains.title: Transparency, Explainability & Accountability
domains.summary: Demands algorithmic inspectability through standardized Model Factsheets, verifiable clinical explainability maps (heatmaps/Grad-CAM), and tamper-evident audit logs.
keyStatutes: National Strategy for AI (NSAI) - NITI Aayog
Draft Indian AI Governance Framework - MeitY
Right to Information (RTI) Act (Algorithmic transparency considerations)
internationalGuidance: ISO/IEC 42001: Artificial Intelligence Management System
OECD AI Transparency and Explainability Principles
Google Model Cards / Partnership on AI Factsheets
criticalRisks: Opaque 'Black Box' inference preventing clinicians from validating anatomical reasons for alerts.
Absence of audit logging in medical negligence disputes.
Unverified marketing claims regarding model architectures and parameter counts.
recommendedClauses: Model Factsheet Submission: The bidder must furnish a comprehensive Model Card detailing parameter count, training set demographics, known edge failure cases, and hardware specifications.
Visual Explainability: For radiological and morphological triage, the system must provide verifiable visual heatmaps (e.g., Grad-CAM) highlighting anatomical regions of algorithmic suspicion.

domains.title: Regulatory & Institutional Considerations
domains.summary: Verifies statutory licensing under Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) Medical Device Rules (MDR 2017) as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Institutional Ethics Committee clearance.
keyStatutes: Medical Device Rules (MDR 2017) under Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940
CDSCO Classification of Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Notice
ICMR National Ethical Guidelines for Biomedical and Health Research
internationalGuidance: IMDRF Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Harmonization
US FDA 510(k) / De Novo Medical Device Clearances
EU MDR 2017/745 CE Mark Certification
criticalRisks: Procurement of unapproved diagnostic software operating under fraudulent 'Research Use Only' claims in clinical care.
Civil and criminal liability for state health officials procuring unregulated SaMD.
Unapproved clinical pilots conducted without ICMR-registered Institutional Ethics Committee oversight.
recommendedClauses: Statutory CDSCO Licensing: Bidder must furnish valid CDSCO Form MD-15 (Import License) or Form MD-5 / MD-9 (Manufacturing License) classified as Class B or Class C Software as a Medical Device.
Ethics Undertaking: All preliminary pilot validation data submitted in technical bids must carry formal approval from an ICMR-registered Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC).

domains.title: Implementation Readiness, Contracting, SLAs & Monitoring
domains.summary: Establishes long-term lifecycle governance, post-market algorithmic drift surveillance, uptime Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and transparent Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) budgeting.
keyStatutes: GeM General Terms and Conditions (GTC) on SLA & Liquidated Damages
GFR 2017 Rule 172 (Performance Security) and Rule 225 (Contract Management)
National Health Mission State PIP Financial Guidelines
internationalGuidance: ISO/IEC 23894: Artificial Intelligence - Risk Management
NHS England Post-Deployment Algorithm Monitoring Protocol
WHO Guidance on Total Cost of Ownership for Digital Health
criticalRisks: Undetected algorithmic performance drift over time due to seasonal diseases or sensor degradation.
Crippling unbudgeted recurring per-scan fees and exorbitant hardware vendor lock-in.
Lack of designated state-level training resulting in abandoned edge terminals.
recommendedClauses: Mandatory Algorithmic Drift Recalibration: Vendor shall perform semi-annual drift audits and model recalibrations at zero additional cost throughout the 3-year contract lifecycle.

Exit Management & Data Handover: Upon contract expiry or termination, vendor shall transfer all state clinical inference logs, annotations, and system telemetry in open standard format within 30 days.
